ava.s: Heads-up — Reef POC seeing two issues on embeddings->rerank: dims mismatch and intermittent 429s. Can someone triage?

lucas.se: On it. Exact errors? model names?

ava.s: From customer: `Error: Invalid vector dimension: expected 1536 but got 768` and `HTTP 429: rate_limited`. They said encoder client is v0.9.1, calling POST /v1/embeddings then POST /v1/rerank. Model string they pass: `open-embed-compat`.

priyaa.support: Ask for request payload and any server trace IDs.

ava.s: Sample (redacted):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{"model":"open-embed-compat","input":["doc A","doc B"],"batch_size":16}
```

mateo.runtime: Likely encoder produces 768 while our reranker expects 1536. Check model metadata: `GET /v1/models/open-embed-compat` — look for "embedding_dim". Also 429s at batch=16 probably hitting per-tenant concurrency throttle; try batch_size=8 as workaround.

lucas.se: Also ask if they use a local sentence-transformers model (all-MiniLM -> 768). Could be alias confusion.

priyaa.support: Pulled trace trc_0a1b2c3: `ERROR rerank-validator: expected_dim=1536 got=768 request_id=req_7f9`

ava.s: Customer admits they used an on-prem all-MiniLM encoder. They tested our hosted `open-embed-1536` and rerank accepted vectors.

lucas.se: Root cause = encoder model mismatch. Action: give customer curl to inspect model metadata and recommend batch_size<=8.

ava.s: Sent curl and suggested test commands.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-4721 to temporarily raise per-tenant concurrency for reef-poc (+2) for 48h.

mateo.runtime: Approved short burst; but recommend client-side chunking and exponential backoff for retries.

ava.s: Customer tried batch_size=8 and succeeded with our hosted encoder. They're switching encoder to 1536 variant. I'll update POC playbook with a checklist: verify embedding_dim early, include curl snippet, and default to batch_size 8.

priyaa.support: Leaving ticket INF-4721 open until burst expires.

lucas.se: Filing docs PR for checklist.

ava.s: Thanks all :thumbsup:
